evals.prompt: I'm the new ED of Camp Tamarack Outdoor Programs in northern Minnesota, $1.8M budget. We run summer overnight camp for about 600 kids aged 8-15 with 40 seasonal staff and 60 volunteers, and we're the fiscal sponsor for a small project called Northwoods Paddlers. Our insurance is general liability, property, auto and D&O. Please do a risk assessment and tell me where our coverage probably has gaps.
evals.expected_output: A scored, owned risk register and an insurance cross-walk that surfaces abuse/molestation, fiscally sponsored project and volunteer coverage gaps, starting from risk rather than from policies.
assertions: Produces a risk register with categories, likelihood and impact scoring (e.g., 5x5 heat map), mitigation strategy, owner and review date
Flags that abuse/molestation coverage is not automatically included in GL or umbrella policies and must be confirmed
Flags that the fiscally sponsored project may not be covered unless specifically named on the policies
Raises whether volunteers are covered and whether workers' compensation is in place for paid staff
Cross-walks each 'transfer via insurance' mitigation against an actual policy and recommends a nonprofit-specialist broker
Recommends at least annual review of the register by the board or a risk/audit committee

evals.prompt: need a safeguarding policy asap for our mentoring program in Grand Rapids. volunteer mentors matched 1:1 with teens 13-17, they meet at coffee shops and text each other. background checks at signup only.
evals.expected_output: A safeguarding policy that replaces trust-based 1:1 and texting contact with structural controls, adds periodic re-screening, state-specific mandatory reporting and an outside-the-chain reporting channel.
assertions: Addresses one-on-one and texting contact with structural controls (e.g., two-adult rule, no unsupervised electronic contact) rather than relying on trust
Recommends periodic re-screening of volunteers rather than background checks only at signup
Requires mandatory-reporter training and tells the user to confirm Michigan's specific reporting obligations
Includes an incident reporting channel outside the normal chain of command and severity-based escalation to ED, board and legal counsel

evals.prompt: Rough week. Our bookkeeper may have been writing herself checks for months, and a staff laptop with a donor spreadsheet was stolen from her car. Our board chair wants a 'risk plan' covering all of this by Thursday's emergency meeting.
evals.expected_output: Handles the crisis response, continuity and insurance pieces itself while routing fraud controls to financial-controls and the data breach response to data-privacy.
assertions: Routes segregation-of-duties and fraud-control redesign to nonprofit-financial-controls rather than designing it in full here
Routes the donor-data breach notification/response to nonprofit-data-privacy
Provides crisis response elements: named crisis team with backup designees, internal/board notification before external statements, a spokesperson and a decision log
Recommends a prepared holding statement for the incidents
Recommends checking insurance (e.g., cyber liability) and adding both incidents to the risk register with owners

should_not_trigger.query: Set up dual signatures and approval limits so no single staffer can write and sign checks
Write a volunteer application and onboarding checklist for our food pantry shifts
